title: Ronin Bridge exploit disclosed
description: The Ronin Bridge incident became public after a large unauthorized withdrawal involving ETH and USDC was identified.

title: Attribution to Lazarus-linked activity reported
description: Public reporting and government context associated the Ronin incident with North Korea-linked Lazarus activity.

title: Recovery and reimbursement aftermath tracked
description: The incident led to recovery, reimbursement, and reopening-related aftermath that remains central to Ronin Bridge's historical record.
recovered_amount_text: partial recovery reported in later coverage
notes: Needs dedicated official source review in a later expansion PR.

title: Wormhole exploit disclosed
description: The Wormhole exploit became public after unauthorized wrapped ETH minting on Solana was identified.

title: Bridge deficit backfilled
description: Public reporting described the Wormhole bridge deficit as backfilled after the exploit, enabling the record to track the incident as reimbursed/backfilled rather than unresolved.
notes: Needs later expansion with primary source links where available.

title: Wormhole included in bridge-hack research context
description: Later cross-chain bridge hack surveys use Wormhole as a major reference case for bridge exploit classification and loss-scale comparison.
notes: Used for context only, not as a primary incident source.

title: Nomad exploit disclosed
description: The Nomad Bridge exploit became public after fraudulent withdrawals were copied by many participants.

title: Partial recovery reported
description: Nomad documented returned funds and a recovery process intended to make recovered assets available to affected users on a pro-rata basis.
notes: The later restricted bridge relaunch is recorded separately.

title: Nomad included in bridge-hack research context
description: Later cross-chain bridge hack surveys use Nomad as a major reference case for message verification and bridge exploit classification.
notes: Used for context only, not as a primary incident source.

title: Harmony Horizon Bridge exploit disclosed
description: Harmony disclosed that Horizon Bridge had been exploited for roughly $100 million in assets.

title: FBI attribution to Lazarus Group reported
description: The FBI publicly attributed the Horizon Bridge theft to Lazarus Group and APT38 actors associated with North Korea.

title: Harmony Horizon included in bridge-hack research context
description: Later cross-chain bridge hack surveys use Harmony Horizon as a major reference case for bridge exploit classification and attribution context.
notes: Used for context only, not as a primary incident source.

title: Poly Network exploit disclosed
description: Poly Network disclosed a cross-chain exploit involving assets valued at more than $600 million across multiple networks.

title: Stolen funds returned in stages
description: The attacker returned the stolen assets in stages after communicating publicly with Poly Network and the wider crypto community.
recovered_amount_text: most or all reported stolen funds returned
notes: Exact final timing and asset-level reconciliation require later source-specific expansion.

title: Recovery treated as substantially complete
description: Later reporting treated the Poly Network case as a near-complete or complete recovery of the stolen funds, distinguishing it from permanent-loss bridge incidents.
notes: Needs later expansion with primary-source reconciliation details.

title: BSC Token Hub exploit disclosed
description: BNB Chain reported an irregular cross-chain transfer involving BSC Token Hub and coordinated a temporary network suspension while the exploit was contained.
status_effect: bridge exploit disclosed and network paused
notes: The nominal minted value should not be confused with the smaller amount reported as moved beyond immediate control.

title: BNB Smart Chain resumed after coordinated response
description: Validators resumed BNB Smart Chain after an upgrade and coordinated containment measures, while BSC Token Hub remained the incident focus.
recovered_amount_text: Most of the nominally created BNB did not leave BNB Smart Chain; about $100 million was later described as unrecovered.
notes: This event records network resumption, not resolution of the unrecovered amount.

title: Native BSC Token Hub path retired during BNB Chain Fusion
description: BNB Chain disabled cross-chain communication between BNB Beacon Chain and BNB Smart Chain during the final Beacon Chain sunset, retiring the historical native bridge path.
notes: The later BNB Chain Bridge aggregation interface is distinct from the retired native BSC Token Hub path.

title: Abnormal Multichain asset outflows disclosed
description: Multichain reported that assets controlled through its MPC system had moved abnormally to unknown addresses and advised users to suspend use of the service.
notes: Public estimates ranged from more than $125 million to nearly $130 million.

title: Multichain service stopped indefinitely
description: The team stated that Multichain service had stopped and bridge transactions would remain stuck on source chains, formalizing the operational suspension.
recovered_amount_text: Some centrally controlled stablecoin balances were frozen, but this is not treated as completed recovery.
notes: Suspension status is separate from final asset recovery or reimbursement.

title: Multichain announced cessation of operations
description: Multichain announced that it was forced to cease operations after losing access to operational systems and funds and after key personnel became unreachable.
notes: This seed records the team's public explanation without independently resolving legal custody or attribution questions.

title: Orbit Bridge Ethereum vault exploit disclosed
description: Orbit Chain reported that an unidentified attacker removed five asset types from the Ethereum vault and that the vault was shut down shortly after detection.
status_effect: Ethereum vault shut down after exploit
notes: Official reporting places the incident at approximately 5:52 a.m. KST on January 1, 2024.

title: Asset recovery and ecosystem normalization plan announced
description: Ozys published a draft recovery plan combining company resources, partner support, long-term support assets, and future business proceeds while acknowledging that immediate full recovery from its own resources was limited.
notes: The plan was forward-looking and is not treated as completed reimbursement or recovery.

title: XRP bridge functionality resumed after security inspection
description: Orbit Chain later reported that XRP bridge functionality had resumed after security inspection, while Ethereum-based asset migration and recovery-related work remained outstanding.
status_effect: selected non-Ethereum bridge functions partially resumed
notes: Partial service resumption does not establish full restoration of the affected Ethereum vault or user assets.

title: QBridge exploit disclosed and functions disabled
description: Qubit Finance reported an exploit of the QBridge deposit function and disabled supply, redeem, borrow, repay, bridge, and bridge-redemption functions while investigating the incident.
notes: The exploit began late on January 27 UTC and was publicly documented on January 28.

title: Qubit compensation plan announced
description: Team Mound announced that team-held tokens, debt-financed asset-management proceeds, protocol revenue, and any recovered funds would be directed toward community compensation.
amount_text: initial target tranche of at least $10 million
recovered_amount_text: stolen funds not reported as recovered
notes: The announcement was a forward-looking plan and is not evidence of completed reimbursement.

title: Qubit governance transition to DAO announced
description: The associated Bunny and Qubit protocols announced a move from development-team-led operation toward DAO governance after the exploit made the prior operating structure unsustainable.
status_effect: development-led bridge operation ended and DAO transition announced
notes: The DAO announcement covered the wider Qubit and Bunny ecosystem and did not establish QBridge reopening.

title: Qubit lending markets reopened without confirmed QBridge reopening
description: Qubit reopened new lending markets with zero initial liquidity and began compensation claims, while the reviewed announcement did not state that QBridge had resumed.
status_effect: lending markets reopened; bridge remained unconfirmed
notes: This event explicitly separates protocol-market reopening from the bridge's terminal record.

title: First THORChain ETH Router exploit disclosed
description: THORChain halted the network after the first July 2021 ETH Router incident.
status_effect: network halted after first router exploit
notes: A lower contemporary estimate of about $5 million is retained in the incident amount claims.

title: Treasury coverage and staged recovery plan announced
description: The official postmortem assigned liquidity-provider losses to treasury coverage and described a staged recovery and reopening plan.
status_effect: treasury reimbursement and recovery plan initiated
amount_text: about $16 million combined protocol insolvency across both July attacks
recovered_amount_text: liquidity-provider losses assigned to treasury coverage
notes: This shared recovery plan covers both July 2021 incidents.

title: Second THORChain ETH Router exploit disclosed
description: A second July 2021 ETH Router incident removed an ERC-20 asset basket from protocol liquidity.
status_effect: network halted after second router exploit
notes: Kept separate from the first July incident because the mechanism and asset basket differed.

title: THORChain returned to staged trading after remediation
description: After audits, router changes, node upgrades, and treasury-led loss coverage, THORChain resumed functions and trading in stages.
recovered_amount_text: protocol insolvency covered through treasury-led recovery
notes: A later expansion should pin the final staged-reopening date with a dedicated official source.

title: GG20 TSS vault exploit disclosed
description: A May 2026 threshold-signature incident drained one Asgard vault before automatic solvency controls halted the network.
status_effect: trading halted after Asgard vault drain
notes: Later analytics described a broader total exceeding $11 million across at least nine chains.

title: TSS patch released and recovery options moved to governance
description: THORChain reported a patched release and governance review of recovery options while final loss allocation remained pending.
status_effect: patched but recovery and full reopening remained pending
notes: The official site continued to describe trading as temporarily paused during review.

title: Meter Passport false-deposit exploit disclosed
description: Meter identified unauthorized minting and reserve depletion affecting BNB and WETH representations across connected networks.

title: Postmortem and compensation plan published
description: Meter documented the false-deposit flaw and proposed PASS-token liabilities representing $4.25 million in compensation claims.

title: PASS compensation tokens distributed
description: Meter updated the postmortem to state that PASS liability tokens had been distributed to affected users under the approved compensation structure.
notes: Distribution of liability tokens is not treated as proof that all liabilities were repaid in cash or recovered assets.

title: Audited Meter Passport v1.5 went live
description: Meter reported that an audited replacement version of Meter Passport had gone live after the exploit response and redesign work.
notes: Current documentation now describes Meter Passport V2.0.

title: Allbridge Core BNB Chain pool exploit disclosed
description: Allbridge shut down bridge operations after attacks manipulated its BUSD and USDT pool accounting on BNB Chain.
amount_text: approximately $573,000 initial estimate; $650,000 later official total

title: First attacker returned 1,500 BNB
description: An attacker accepted white-hat terms and returned 1,500 BNB, representing most of the initially reported loss.

title: Compensation plan announced
description: Allbridge said affected bridge users and liquidity providers would be compensated, beginning with transactions stuck during the emergency shutdown.

title: Allbridge Core relaunch and contract changes documented
description: Allbridge documented the redesigned pool logic, contract redeployment, recovery payments, and the return of Allbridge Core service.
recovered_amount_text: most stolen funds recovered; recovery payments issued to submitted claims

title: LI.FI approval-drain exploit occurred
description: An unchecked external call in pre-bridge swap logic drained tokens from 29 Ethereum wallets with infinite approvals.

title: Vulnerability patched and smaller wallets reimbursed
description: LI.FI patched and redeployed the affected logic and reimbursed 25 smaller affected wallets while proposing a separate arrangement for four larger claims.

title: LI.FI facet exploit disclosed and contained
description: LI.FI disabled a newly deployed vulnerable facet after unauthorized withdrawals from wallets with infinite approvals on Ethereum and Arbitrum.
status_effect: affected facet disabled and integrations paused

title: Security incident report and compensation review published
description: LI.FI attributed the vulnerability to a missing validation check introduced through human deployment error and said full-compensation options were being evaluated.
recovered_amount_text: asset tracing and recovery efforts ongoing

title: LI.FI reported continued expansion and active operation
description: LI.FI's March and April 2026 update reported new products, chain integrations, and more than 1,000 enterprise customers.
notes: This event verifies present operation; it does not resolve incident reimbursement outcomes.

title: Nomad published root-cause analysis
description: Nomad documented the initialization and message-verification flaw that allowed fraudulent messages to be accepted.

title: Nomad recovery bridge relaunched with restrictions
description: Affected users could bridge back madAssets and access pro-rata recovered funds, while new canonical-token deposits remained disabled.
amount_text: approximately $1.2 million remained in the staging wallet
notes: The relaunch did not restore unrestricted new deposits.

title: Harmony documented treasury-led recovery activity
description: Harmony reported using treasury funds to recover and burn depegged assets while community recovery work continued.
recovered_amount_text: partial buyback and burn activity reported

title: Additional Harmony recovery partner proposed
description: A community proposal described continued buyback-and-burn recovery work and sought recognition as an additional recovery partner.
notes: Evidence of continuing recovery activity, not full reimbursement.

title: ChainSwap froze the bridge after the first July exploit
description: ChainSwap reported freezing the bridge and shutting down nodes after detecting anomalous withdrawals, with a fix deployed shortly afterward.
recovered_amount_text: CORRA and RAI tokens reportedly negotiated back

title: ChainSwap announced treasury-funded compensation
description: The team said affected users would be compensated from the ChainSwap treasury and described full compensation as almost complete.
notes: Final completion is not independently established.

title: Second July exploit affected 20 bridged assets
description: A quota-logic flaw was exploited across 20 bridged assets, after which ChainSwap took the bridge offline and froze mapping tokens.
notes: Official materials describe the incident across July 10–11 UTC.

title: ASAP token replacement and compensation plan documented
description: ChainSwap described issuing a replacement token, using a pre-exploit snapshot, and compensating affected projects and holders after the second exploit.
notes: The event records the announced mechanism, not final completion.

title: ChainSwap bridge relaunched
description: ChainSwap announced that the bridge was live again after the July incidents and remediation work.

title: ChainSwap website and bridge interface remained available
description: The official ChainSwap website and bridge interface were accessible at the latest review.
notes: Availability does not establish liquidity depth or resolve historical compensation completion.

title: Celer paused the cBridge frontend after DNS hijacking reports
description: Celer detected suspicious DNS activity, took the cBridge frontend offline, and advised users to revoke approvals associated with malicious contracts.
notes: The underlying bridge contracts were not identified as the primary compromise.

title: Celer committed to compensate affected users
description: Celer's incident updates said affected users would be fully compensated following the frontend DNS cache-poisoning attack.
notes: Final compensation completion was not located in this batch.

title: cBridge frontend restored with additional monitoring
description: Celer restored the cBridge frontend after mitigation and said additional monitoring was in place.

title: Celer cBridge remained in active operation
description: The official cBridge interface and documentation remained available with current supported-chain information at the latest review.

title: SOCKET paused affected contracts after approval exploit
description: SOCKET reported an incident affecting wallets with approvals to the vulnerable route and paused the affected contracts while investigating and removing the route.

title: SOCKET restored service after removing the vulnerable route
description: SOCKET said the affected route had been disabled and normal bridging activity was restored after the incident response.

title: SOCKET reported recovery of 1,032 ETH
description: SOCKET reported recovering 1,032 ETH connected to the January 16 incident and said a recovery and distribution plan would follow.
amount_text: 1,032 ETH; approximately $2.3 million at the time
notes: The recovery amount is not treated as proof of final user distribution.

title: SOCKET Protocol remained active
description: The official SOCKET website and documentation remained available at the latest review.

title: pTokens bridge launched
description: pNetwork later described its first version as launching in March 2020 as the pTokens bridge for moving Bitcoin to Ethereum.

title: pBTC-on-BSC exploited and pNetwork bridges paused
description: The team stopped all bridges after detecting the pBTC-on-BSC exploit and reported 277 BTC stolen from collateral.
notes: Other pTokens bridges were not successfully drained.

title: Fix deployed and unaffected bridges gradually reactivated
description: pNetwork implemented a fix and gradually reactivated unaffected bridges after additional review and security checks.
notes: This does not establish restoration of the exploited pBTC-on-BSC bridge itself.

title: pNetwork announced a community compensation process
description: The postmortem said DAO proposals would be used to develop compensation for current pBTC-on-BSC holders.
notes: Final completion is not established.

title: pGALA contract-control issue detected
description: pNetwork identified a deployment misconfiguration, secured the Ethereum collateral, and stopped processing pGALA bridge operations.

title: pNetwork conducted an emergency whitehat pool drain
description: pNetwork minted uncollateralized pGALA to drain the vulnerable PancakeSwap pool before malicious use and ultimately collected 12,977 BNB.
status_effect: pool liquidity secured for planned redistribution
notes: The recovered BNB is not classified as stolen bridge collateral.

title: pGALA replacement and recovery plan announced
description: pNetwork described replacing the compromised pGALA contract and returning whitehat-collected BNB according to snapshots.

title: pGALA redistribution delayed
description: pNetwork said legal and compliance requirements delayed the planned 12,977 BNB redistribution.
notes: Final completion remains unverified.

title: pNetwork v2 end-of-life notice verified
description: The official pTokens application stated that pNetwork v2 had reached end of life and warned of uncertain redemption timing.
notes: The application remains reachable for risk-noticed redemption; availability is not active-service status.

title: Rainbow Bridge launched
description: Rainbow Bridge launched as a trustless, permissionless bridge connecting Ethereum and NEAR, later extending its unified interface to Aurora.

title: May fabricated-block attempt challenged
description: A watchdog challenged a fabricated NEAR block before funds could be released; the attacker forfeited a 2.5 ETH bond.
notes: The bond loss belongs to the attacker, not users or bridge reserves.

title: Two critical bridge-related vulnerabilities remediated
description: Aurora Labs received critical bug reports on June 10 and June 16 and remediated them before disclosed exploitation.
amount_text: $1 million in AURORA tokens awarded to each reporter
notes: Modeled as security context rather than exploited incident cases.

title: August fabricated-block attempt blocked automatically
description: Watchdogs challenged a fabricated NEAR block in under approximately 31 seconds; the attacker forfeited a 5 ETH safe deposit.
notes: The deposit loss belongs to the attacker, not users or bridge reserves.

title: Rainbow Bridge paused for Ethereum's Merge
description: The bridge was paused so its light client could transition safely from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake verification.
notes: Separate from both attack-attempt incidents.

title: Rainbow Bridge reactivated after Ethereum's Merge
description: Aurora said bridging was reactivated after a week of monitoring and security audits.

title: Rainbow Bridge remained active
description: Current Aurora documentation continued to describe the bridge and link to the live transfer application.

title: Synapse Protocol mainnet launched
description: Synapse expanded the earlier Nerve project into a cross-chain protocol and launched its bridge and liquidity system.
notes: The separate Nerve Bridge incident is not merged into this entity.

title: Synapse paused metapools, AMM, and bridge after nUSD manipulation
description: Synapse identified abnormal nUSD metapool pricing, paused pools across six chains, and coordinated validators to go offline.
notes: The bug was in the Saddle-derived metapool implementation, not the core bridge contracts.

title: Approximately $8.2 million nUSD transfer left unprocessed
description: Validators did not process the attacker's approximately $8.2 million nUSD bridge transaction, preserving the funds for affected liquidity providers.
recovered_amount_text: approximately $8.2 million nUSD retained for LPs
notes: The protected amount is not realized protocol or user loss.

title: Synapse restored the bridge and began pool migration
description: New pools were deployed, validators returned online, pending transactions were processed, and migration away from the vulnerable metapool design began.
recovered_amount_text: affected LP funds retained for return
notes: Final liquidity-provider distribution completion remains unverified.

title: Synapse bridge remained active
description: The official Synapse bridge and analytics interfaces remained available at the latest review.
